chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not take wealth for trade (mudarabah) except wealth upon which you pay zakat or its owner pays zakat.
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If there are goods with you in the house, stored away, and you are given capital for them, but you turn away from selling them, then upon you is their zakat.'

key_terms.مُضَارَبَةً: Trade partnership or capital taken for trading

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat ruling for trade goods held in storage that are not sold?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that zakat on trade goods (mal al-tijarah) is obligatory regardless of whether the goods are actively sold or merely held in storage, emphasizing the purification of capital. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the mere possession of capital intended for trade triggers the zakat obligation, ensuring financial integrity in commercial transactions. The hadith serves as a practical guideline for merchants to maintain spiritual and economic purity in their assets.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘Do not be taking wealth for trading except wealth which you purify (pay Zakāt on) or its owner purifies it (pays Zakāt on)’.
And heasws said: ‘If there were goods with you in the house, for which you are given the capital of your wealth, but you turn away from it, so upon you is its Zakāt’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Do not accept an asset for profit-sharing business unless you pay its Zakat or the shareholder pays.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘If you have an asset in stock in your home for which you are offered payment for your capital but you ignored to receive it, you are required to pay its Zakat.’”
